Waking up with a sore jaw, headaches or worn-down teeth? 😬

You may be clenching or grinding in your sleep, and very often the source is a bite that's off. When your teeth don't meet evenly, your jaw muscles work overtime: wearing enamel, cracking teeth and straining the jaw joint (TMJ).

Think of it like your feet. A drugstore insole is one-size-fits-all. A custom orthotic is made for YOUR foot. Same with your bite: a custom oral orthotic is built to balance your bite so your muscles can finally relax.

The tooth is gone. The gum healed. But what's happening in the bone underneath? 🦴

After an extraction, the socket should fill with new bone. Sometimes it doesn't, leaving a hollow pocket of poorly healed bone with poor blood flow, and sometimes chronic inflammation or infection (osteomyelitis). In biological dentistry we call these cavitations.

They can hide on a standard 2D x-ray. A 3D CBCT scan gives us a much better look, and then we confirm with a clinical exam.

Healed on top isn't always healed inside.

"Your labs are normal." But you still feel off? 🔬

What your labs aren't telling you: about 99% of your body's magnesium lives inside your cells and bones. Less than 1% is in your blood serum. So a "normal" serum level may not show what your cells are actually holding.

And reference ranges are population averages, not your personal best. You can sit inside the lines and still feel off.

This isn't medical advice, just a better question to bring to your provider.

Can root canal bacteria travel? 🦷

Dentin is full of microscopic tubules, and bacteria can get deep inside them. Even after a good root canal, some can remain. Studies have measured bacteria entering the blood during treatment (Debelian 1995; Savarrio 2005).

Links to heart disease are weak and show up mostly in men 40 and under. Linked isn't the same as caused, and the science isn't settled.

📅 Ask us for a calm second look, link in bio.

Snoring isn't just noise. It can be your airway closing. 😴

In obstructive sleep apnea, the tongue and soft palate collapse and breathing STOPS. Oxygen drops. Your body panics: adrenaline surges, heart rate and blood pressure spike, and your brain jolts you awake just enough to breathe. Over and over, all night, usually without you remembering.

What that feels like in real life:
• Waking up exhausted no matter how long you slept
• Morning headaches
• Brain fog, short fuse, low mood
• Getting up at night to pee
• Grinding your teeth

Over time, untreated sleep apnea is linked to high blood pressure, heart disease and diabetes.

Only a sleep study can tell for sure. We can help you start with a home screening. 📅 Link in bio.

#sleepapnea #airwayhealth #snoring #biologicaldentistry #sleephealth

Bad breath usually isn't your teeth. 👅

Most of it comes from the back of your tongue. Bacteria that hate oxygen hide in that coating, break down proteins and release sulfur gases. That's the smell.

What makes it worse:
• Dry mouth and mouth breathing
• Gum pockets, where the same bacteria live below the gumline
• Tonsil stones

Mints and sprays just mask it for a few minutes. Harsh antiseptic rinses wipe out your good bacteria too.

What actually helps:
• Clean your tongue every day (scraper, back to front)
• Sip water and breathe through your nose
• Get your gums checked

If your mouth is healthy and it still persists, we look further (sinus, reflux and more).

📅 Ask about a fresh-breath & gum check, link in bio.

The sooner we look, the more options you have.

Your mouth isn't supposed to be sterile. 🦠

How your good bacteria protect you:
• Streptococcus salivarius & S. sanguinis crowd out harmful species, release natural antimicrobials and help buffer acid
• Rothia, Neisseria & Veillonella turn nitrates from leafy greens and beets into nitric oxide, which helps relax blood vessels and support healthy blood pressure
• You swallow about a liter of saliva a day: your oral biome helps seed your gut biome

The troublemakers: Streptococcus mutans (cavities) and P. gingivalis, T. denticola & T. forsythia (gum disease).

⚠️ Antiseptic mouthwash doesn't pick sides. In a 2013 study, one week of chlorhexidine rinse lowered oral nitrite and raised blood pressure (Kapil et al., Free Radical Biology & Medicine). In a 2020 study, using mouthwash twice a day or more was linked to a higher risk of developing hypertension (Joshipura et al., Blood Pressure).

Other biome disruptors:
• Frequent sugar & constant snacking
• Alcohol/antiseptic rinses
• Antibiotics
• Mouth breathing & dry mouth (including from medications)
• Smoking & vaping
• Stress & poor sleep

Bacteria light the match; your terrain decides if it becomes a candle or a wildfire.

📅 Ask about oral microbiome testing, link in bio.

#oralmicrobiome #nitricoxide #guthealth #biologicaldentistry #holistichealth

Sometimes it's mineral balance, not motivation.

This isn't medical advice, it's an invitation to get curious before you white-knuckle another diet.

Your enamel repairs itself every day, if you give it the right conditions. ✨

🧪 The pH story: every sugary or acidic bite drops your mouth's pH. Below about 5.5, enamel starts to dissolve. Saliva brings the pH back up and puts minerals back, but that takes 30–60 minutes. Constant snacking and sipping means your teeth never get to recover.

My remineralization picks:
• Nano-hydroxyapatite toothpaste (Boka or RiseWell), twice a day: the same mineral your enamel is made of
• Xylitol (Spry or Xlear), 4–5 times a day: keeps pH up and starves acid-making bacteria. It's the frequency that counts.

Early white spots can often heal. 📅 Ask for our remineralization kit, link in bio.

Transparency: we carry some of these products in our office and may earn a small margin.

#hydroxyapatite #remineralization #xylitol #biologicaldentistry #holisticdentist

The tooth is gone. The gum healed. But what's happening in the bone underneath? 🦴

After an extraction, the socket should fill with new bone. Sometimes it doesn't, leaving a hollow pocket of poorly healed bone with poor blood flow, and sometimes chronic inflammation or infection (osteomyelitis). In biological dentistry we call these cavitations.

They can hide on a standard 2D x-ray. A 3D CBCT scan gives us a much better look, and then we confirm with a clinical exam.

Healed on top isn't always healed inside.

📅 Ask about a 3D CBCT evaluation, link in bio.

Healing with your own blood. 🩸✨

PRF (platelet-rich fibrin) is made from a small sample of YOUR blood:
1️⃣ We draw a small amount, like a routine blood test
2️⃣ It's spun in a centrifuge, with nothing added
3️⃣ It forms a natural fibrin clot packed with platelets, white blood cells and growth factors
4️⃣ We place it in the extraction socket or graft site, where it releases those growth factors over several days

Studies link PRF to more comfortable healing and fewer dry sockets after extractions. It supports what your body already knows how to do.

No additives. Just you.

→ Heavy metals interfering with absorption

3 years using HTMA in my biological dental practice.

550+ prescription medications list dry mouth as a side effect.

Dry mouth = no saliva = no enamel remineralization = accelerated decay.

Most dentists prescribe Biotène.

additionalPosts.text:

→ Mouth breathing (dries tissues every night)

Saliva does: remineralize enamel, buffer acid, fight bacteria, protect gum tissue.

Lose it and everything accelerates.

→ Myofunctional therapy for mouth breathing
→ Medication review with prescriber
→ Mineral optimization
→ Nasal hygiene protocol

Not Biotène.

Dry mouth is a signal. Treat the signal.

3 mistakes I made in my first year implementing AI at PJN Dental.

I'm sharing them because I see other dentists making the same ones:

Mistake 1: Started with the shiny pod instead of the painful one.
My biggest time drain was clinical notes. But I started with patient recall messaging because it felt exciting. Six weeks of mediocre results before I redirected.

Mistake 2: Treated AI output as final output.
An AI system hallucinated content in a summary note. It never reached a patient — but it would have if I hadn't built in a mandatory review step. AI drafts. Humans decide. Non-negotiable.

Mistake 3: Bought the tool, skipped the workflow.
ChatGPT alone isn't a system. The difference between dentists getting results and those who aren't is the workflow around the tool, not the tool itself.

The sequence: Map your workflow → identify the AI slot → build the review step → then automate.
